notes:
Self-overlap within one editable fill, improved hole creation, and safer travel routing.

- Keep a closed Tatami or Satin fill as ONE object while its two internal sections overlap. Select two outline nodes across the join and choose Edit > Set Self Overlap Seam. Properties > Reverse order swaps which section sews underneath.
- Shared outline editing and stitch settings survive switching between Tatami and Satin. All section underlay is placed before the final cover.
- Press Enter to close a hole. Improved hole selection and subtraction within overlapping material.
- Improved detection of short exposed travel runs, using actual later stitch coverage. Protect Exposed Travel uses trim/jump moves where a sewn connector cannot be concealed.
- Object previews and markers now follow the same protected plan as the stitch player and export.
- Updated the Resource Guide with step-by-step self-overlap instructions.

Self-overlap currently uses one internal seam and two individually valid sections. Keep the seam beside holes rather than through them. Projects using this feature require v0.2.220 or later. Existing projects retain their saved routing setting; enable Design > Routing > Protect Exposed Travel when needed.

Includes the integrated auto-digitizing and photo tools. Verified offline, including EXP conversion; physical stitch-out testing is not included. Full Satin parity work continues.
